:::{#exr-generalization-error}
#### Score a fitted model on a car it has not seen

A [prediction rule](#def-prediction-rule) $\fitted$
has been fitted to a [training set](#def-training-set) $\trainset$ of $\nobs$ observations,
such as the 20 training cars of @exr-overfitting.
A new car $(\newpredvar, \newoutvar)$ is then drawn from the same population,
independently of $\trainset$.

1. Holding $\trainset$ fixed,
   write the average [loss](#def-observation-loss) $\obsloss{*}$
   that $\fitted$ would incur over all such new cars,
   as an expectation.
   Then write it for squared-error loss,
   as the average squared [prediction error](prediction.qmd#def-prediction-error).
2. Which parts of your expression do you know,
   and which do you not know?
3. The training sRMSE of @exr-overfitting
   is the square root of the [training error](#def-training-mse) $\trainerr$ under squared-error loss.
   What does $\trainerr$ use in place of your expectation?

:::
